items.text: Four real forks exist after BSc Computer Science: a direct job, an MCA, an MSc/M.Tech, or a government exam route.

blocks.heading: What AI Is Actually Changing Here

items.text: AI coding assistants have specifically raised the bar for the straight-to-job fork: a candidate who can only write the kind of boilerplate code a junior developer used to write is now competing against tools that do that for free.
The MCA and MSc/M.Tech forks are less directly exposed to this pressure right now, since they buy time to build that deeper skill layer before entering the job market.

Freelance development, consulting, and building your own product are all genuinely open to a BSc CS graduate, this degree carries no glass ceiling on the ownership path the way some regulated fields do.

visuals.heading: Four Real Forks After BSc CS

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The four real forks after BSc CS

rows: Direct job (software/data/support roles)
You have a real portfolio of projects and coding practice already, regardless of what your college taught.
Fastest to income, 0 extra years
MCA (Master of Computer Applications)
You want deeper, structured CS/software training your BSc program did not fully cover, especially from a college where BSc CS leaned more theoretical than applied.
2 extra years
MSc Computer Science or M.Tech (lateral entry where allowed)
You are aiming at research, teaching, or a specialised technical track like AI/ML that rewards a stronger formal research foundation.
2 extra years
A government exam route (banking IT, PSU, SSC technical posts)
You want the stability of a government or PSU role and are prepared for a genuinely competitive, separate exam pipeline.
Variable, often 1-3 attempts across 1-2 years

blocks.heading: Real Pay By Fork
rows: Direct Job: Service-Company Software/Support Role (Entry)
Roughly Rs 3-5 LPA
Direct Job: Service-Company Software/Support Role (Entry)
Roughly Rs 3-5 LPA
Direct job: product-company or strong-portfolio hire (entry)
Roughly Rs 5-9 LPA, occasionally higher with a genuinely strong project portfolio
Post-MCA, product or service-company hire
Roughly Rs 4-7 LPA, a modest premium over a bachelor's-only hire at the same company tier
Post-MSc/M.Tech, specialised technical or research-adjacent role
Roughly Rs 6-12 LPA, with the widest range of the four forks depending on specialisation and employer
Government/PSU IT role (post-exam)
Follows the standard government/PSU pay scale for the specific post, stable but slower-growing than private-sector product roles
